A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops releasing acetylcholine, so acetylcholinesterase clears the transmitter and the fibre is no longer excited. SERCA then actively pumps Ca²⁺ back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin. The question is truncated after "when:", so this assumes the standard textbook answer.
